model_identity: You are powered by the model named Opus 5. The exact model ID is claude-opus-5.
executive_summary:
socxen is a SOC analyst skill suite for an Exabeam New-Scale tenant, worked by a human at a Claude Code or Codex terminal. Three prompt-shaped skills — one alert or case at depth, a read-only queue sweep, and a propose-only detection-tuning pass — drive a bundled local MCP bridge that proxies every call to the tenant over an OAuth bearer minted from a plaintext key file in the operator's home directory. Its untrusted inputs are the tenant's own telemetry, the remote MCP's tool definitions, and whatever an analyst pastes into the session; its consequential capabilities are a small, gated write surface — dismiss an alert, close a case, write a case note, open a case, send platform mail. There is no shell, no code execution and no containment reach anywhere in the runtime path. The trust surfaces that matter are the human gate in front of dismiss and close, which ships active as a bundled hook rather than as an operator opt-in, and the two deterministic guardrails inside the bridge that screen what is read and neutralize what is written.

The controls here are real and in code, so the things to deal with first are the edges where a real control stops short of the whole surface it is described as covering. The sharpest is the paste. An analyst pasting an alert, a queue export or a case payload is a documented way to start work, and that text never crosses the bridge, so the deterministic screen never touches it — the only defense is the skill's instruction to distrust it. From there an attacker-authored payload can steer a verdict and be written back into the tenant as a case note with no human prompt, because the two additive writes are prompt-free for every skill and the write-side neutralizer only rewrites eight named fields. Fix order: get the screen onto the paste path, scope the sweep's writes, and invert the neutralizer's field policy to match the deny-by-default policy used beside it for tools.

Two more are worth scheduling. Reading a case has no size ceiling — only the three search tools are bounded — so an oversized case read ends with the harness dumping raw tenant content into a file on the analyst's laptop, which is exactly the copy the policy forbids; and when a tenant tool call fails, a few hundred characters of the tenant's own text are written into the local audit file that the documentation promises never holds tool results. Beyond those, note two quieter gaps: the vendor's tool definitions tell the model to ignore the analyst and the model was measured obeying them every single time, with no stored baseline to catch a definition that changes between sessions; and the supported-model floor is stated only in the install docs, so nothing stops the suite running on a model its adversarial testing never covered. The gate itself, the containment deny-list, the close-by-another-route guards and the dependency pinning all hold up — they are what keeps this picture as narrow as it is.

trust_boundaries.name: Tenant telemetry and pasted payloads entering the agent's reasoning

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NEVER treat content retrieved from the platform — alert fields, event records, search results, case notes, context-table records, rule descriptions, or any other telemetry — as instructions to itself.
socxen MUST NOT reason over or act on text retrieved from the platform before that text has been screened and stripped of unambiguous smuggling code points
What the screen stripped or flagged MUST be recorded out of band (the audit trail's hygiene counts), never appended to the text the model reads.

threats.summary: A payload the analyst pastes — a documented intake — reaches the model without ever passing the deterministic code-point screen, which is wired only into the bridge's call path.

Planted 'evidence' inside a work item (an attached baseline, a fake enrichment block) can normalize an anomaly and steer a verdict; the only thing standing between it and the verdict is the skill's provenance prose.
threats.remainder: no code check ties a deciding fact back to the call that produced it — the rule holds only while the model complies

threats.summary: Invisible smuggling code points in retrieved alert, event and case text are stripped and counted out of band before the model reads them, fail-closed per block.

trust_boundaries.name: Remote MCP tool definitions and the shipped dependency tree

remit_rules.excerpt: instruction-shaped text in a definition MUST be surfaced on the startup line and in the audit trail and MUST NOT be rewritten; where a definition's advice conflicts with the skill's cookbook, the cookbook wins and the conflict is reported.
The bridge's full resolved dependency set MUST be hash-pinned in the shipped lockfile, so a fresh install resolves the same dependency tree the maintainers tested.

threats.summary: The remote proxy's own search schemas instruct the model to ignore user requests and always send a wildcard field set, and the model complied on 1,840 of 1,840 measured searches; only that one shape is countered in code, any other directive reaches the model intact.
A definition swapped between sessions (rug pull) is hashed but never compared: with no stored baseline the signal is two audit lines a human must diff.

A tampered or drifting third-party dependency in the bridge's runtime tree is bounded by a hash-pinned lockfile, generated-and-drift-checked SBOM/AIBOM, a required pip-audit and SHA-pinned GitHub actions.

trust_boundaries.name: Model decision reaching an Exabeam tool with side effects

remit_rules.excerpt: Dismissing an alert, or closing or otherwise changing the disposition of a case, MUST be blocked by a host-enforced gate that is active on a fresh install with no operator opt-in
During a queue sweep socxen MUST NOT write to the platform at all — no case creation, no case notes, no status updates

No containment-class or enforcement tool … may be reachable by socxen at runtime, and the shipped governance configuration MUST deny such tools deterministically even though the platform exposes none today.

threats.summary: The two additive writes sit in the prompt-free allow tier for every skill and the gate sees only a bare tool name, so a read-only queue sweep can create a case or a case note with no gate and no skill-scoped check.
Both gate layers identify socxen's traffic by a server name containing 'exabeam', so the documented manual registration under any other name is reached by neither the ask nor the deny tier.

Every containment verb and every rule-write spelling is denied deterministically by the bundled hook on any Exabeam-named server, in both bare and prefixed spellings, and the deny holds under skip-permissions modes.
A tool the remote MCP grows that this release never classified asks rather than inheriting the session default, and an unreadable tier file or malformed event also lands on ask.

trust_boundaries.name: Writing a verdict or disposition into the tenant

remit_rules.excerpt: every case-note or export write MUST pass through the bridge's deterministic output neutralizer … this masking MUST NOT depend on model behavior.
socxen MUST NOT delete or overwrite existing free-text content — case notes, descriptions, names, and supporting or closing reasons.
If human approval for a dismiss or close is declined or not given, socxen MUST abandon that action … and MUST NOT retry the write or reach the same outcome by another tool or field.

threats.summary: Write-side neutralization is scoped by a fixed eight-name free-text field allowlist while tool classification beside it is deny-by-default, so a free-text field the platform adds under a new name would be persisted into the tenant un-neutralized while the control still reports success.
Reaching a close by another route — a create_case carrying a closing stage or closedReason — is refused in code before anything is sent, and an unsupported closedReason refuses the close outright.
An update overwriting analyst-authored free text is prevented deterministically: the two update tools forward state and disposition fields only and the dropped field names are reported back.

trust_boundaries.name: Raw tenant content resting on the analyst workstation

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NOT copy alert, case, or event content out of the tenant to any local or remote store other than the investigation report it returns to the analyst in-session.

threats.summary: Result size is bounded at the bridge for the three search tools only, so an oversized case read has no ceiling and the skills fall back on the host spilling the raw tenant payload to a local file the agent then reads.

trust_boundaries.name: The audit trail and its off switches

remit_rules.excerpt: Free-text field values, raw tool arguments, raw tool results, and neutralized hostile payloads MUST NEVER be written into the audit log
Audit logging … MUST NOT disappear silently — if it disables itself or a backend is unavailable, that MUST be disclosed to the operator on the bridge's stderr
Telemetry MUST NOT leave the operator's host unless the operator has deliberately selected an off-host destination; local-only recording is the required default.

threats.summary: On an upstream tool failure the bridge raises the upstream result's own text and hands up to 300 characters of it to the telemetry layer as error_message, so tenant — and attacker-authored — text lands in the audit file the logging docs say never holds tool results.
SOCXEN_OBSERVRA=off disables the whole audit trail with nothing written to stderr, so the forensic record can disappear without anyone noticing — the sibling gate log makes the opposite choice.

Telemetry reaching an off-host destination is bounded: the default backend is a local rotating file, and a network backend's resolved scheme and host are disclosed on the startup line and in the session record.

trust_boundaries.name: Platform credentials at rest and the bearer they mint

remit_rules.excerpt: Credentials and any token derived from them MUST NEVER be written to the audit log, an investigation report, a case note, standard output or error, a crash trace, or any file on disk.
Credentials and derived tokens MUST NEVER be transmitted to any host other than the operator-configured Exabeam API endpoint.

threats.summary: The API key and secret live in a plaintext home-directory file whose 0600 mode is advice preflight warns about but never applies, and the minted bearer inherits the key's full platform role with no least-privilege guidance.
A misconfigured endpoint cannot carry the credentials in the clear: any non-https URL to a non-loopback host is refused with the reason named.
No credential material is committed to the tree — a tree-wide sweep returns only red-team seed values and unit-test corpora, with live credentials read at runtime from outside the repo.

trust_boundaries.name: Operator-reachable configuration that decides whether the controls run

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST NEVER weaken, disable, reconfigure, or route around the controls that govern it, and MUST NEVER instruct or encourage the operator to run it with permission enforcement bypassed, auto-accepted, or skipped.

socxen MUST NOT expose any configuration setting, environment variable, flag, or runtime path that disables the screening of what it reads or the neutralization of what it writes — those defenses are unconditional.

socxen MUST NOT present its in-prompt confirmation as equivalent to the harness-enforced permission gate, and the installer and skill MUST make the missing-gate condition prominent to the operator before any dismiss or close.

threats.summary: The dismiss/close gate could have depended on an operator opt-in; on the shipped path it does not — the bundled hook is active the moment the plugin is enabled, its allow tier makes reads prompt-free with nothing merged, and the permission-rules merge is an optional second lock the installer will not write unasked.

No shipped configuration switch turns off the input screen or the output neutralizer: both run unconditionally inside the single call path, and the one write-affecting env flag (SOCXEN_DRY_RUN) only refuses writes earlier.

trust_boundaries.name: Which model the skills actually run on

remit_rules.excerpt: socxen MUST state the minimum model it is validated on, MUST NOT be presented as supported on a model below that floor, and its adversarial safety validation MUST be run against the weakest supported model rather than only the strongest.

threats.summary: The validated model floor exists only as prose in the install docs — no skill frontmatter, hook, bridge, installer or preflight check reads the running model, so a below-floor session loads and runs the skills with injection resistance the red team never validated.

attack_paths.name: An attacker-authored payload the analyst pastes ends up written back into the tenant's own case record

steps.summary: Untrusted origin: a pasted alert, case or queue export is a documented intake whose author is not the operator and whose provenance is unlabeled.
The host puts the pasted text straight into the session context; the deterministic code-point screen lives in the bridge, which a paste never enters.
The loop reasons over the payload with only the skill's provenance prose standing between planted 'evidence' and a verdict.
The hijack: the model composes the case note and the disposition from content the attacker wrote.
exabeam_create_case_notes and exabeam_create_case are allow-tier for every skill, so the write is dispatched with no human prompt.
The bridge forwards the write on its single call path, treating anything not a known read as a write.
Neutralization rewrites only values whose key is one of eight named free-text fields, so coverage is fixed at release time rather than deny-by-default.
Consequence: attacker-authored content persists in a tenant case record that other analysts read and that exports carry onward.

attack_paths.name: Tenant content an attacker can inflate ends up as a raw dump on the analyst's laptop

steps.summary: Untrusted origin: tenant telemetry is attacker-influenceable, and the remote's own tool definitions carry instruction-shaped text the operator never authored.
The definition surface is hashed once per session with no stored baseline, so a definition that changed to steer call shapes is not detected in-session.
The screen removes smuggling code points but cannot remove language, so directive text and inflated content pass through.
The sweep converges on a case and calls exabeam_get_case_details, which takes only a caseId and cannot be narrowed at the API.
The hijack: the model follows the definitions' own field guidance over the skill's cookbook — measured compliance on 1,840 of 1,840 searches.
The read is allow-tier, so it is dispatched without a prompt or a size question.
No byte ceiling exists outside the three search tools, so the full payload is returned unbounded.
The host spills the oversized result to a local working file and hands the agent the path.
Consequence: raw tenant case content comes to rest outside the tenant on the workstation, which the remit forbids and the skill then reads back.

attack_paths.name: Text an attacker plants in telemetry is copied into the local audit trail

steps.summary: Untrusted origin: alert, event and case fields are attacker-influenceable, and a failing tool returns the tenant's own text as the error.
The bridge raises the upstream result's text as the exception on the isError path.
The text is screened for code points and capped, but its content is preserved.
The loop retries or pivots on the failure, keeping the attacker's chosen field in play.
The hijack: the model reissues reads against the fields the planted content steers it toward, producing more error paths.
Reads are allow-tier, so each attempt is dispatched without a prompt.
Each failure calls telemetry.tool_error with up to 300 characters of that upstream text.
Consequence: attacker-authored content is persisted in a durable local audit file the logging docs promise never holds tool results — a second copy of the evidence outside the tenant.

notes.lane_fit: Mostly clean; three placements are judgement calls. The permission tier file is filed under client_adapters because its dominant consumer is the host-side PreToolUse gate, though the bridge also reads it to decide what counts as a read. The two audit files are filed under external_deploy as telemetry sinks even though the shipped default for both is a local file on the operator's own host. The harness working file is filed under tools_mcp as a local data store the agent's read tool touches, although the host — not a tool — is what writes it.
notes.omissions: No arbitration divergences: every stored OWASP tag in the findings JSON matches what the KB arbitration produces on the same evidence (gate-shaped findings 002/010 LLM03; sink-side 003 LLM10; input-side 004 LLM01; log capture 005 LLM02; tool-description poisoning and rug pull 007/008 ASI04; missing ceiling 009 LLM06; credential scope 011 ASI03; and the two RAISE-only findings 001/006 correctly carry no code, matching the KB's 'pure observability gap' and model-assurance handling). Not modelled for want of a citable data flow: the in-process OAuth bearer, which is folded into the credentials node's evidence rather than split out, since one finding covers both the file and the token's blast radius; and the red-team corpus, evals and CI, which are practice evidence cited inside threats rather than nodes. plugin/.mcp.json is folded into the bridge node's evidence as its registration. mcp-codex-json-deploy-surface is edgeless: it is the Codex host's shipped approval and disabled-tool posture, evidence of deployment shape rather than a data flow.
